decisions.reason: Issue body has no concrete remedy or acceptance contract; local capture and PRS are insufficient.
All stated admission prerequisites match: trusted hash-bound review, scoped authorization, dependencies, and acceptance evidence.
Post-review edits lack a content-hash comparison or renewed attestation.
The producer and decoder share an unpinned serialized contract; parallel membership is unsafe.
Disjoint, independently validated future membership is admissible without changing the active wave.
Parked work requires explicit operator release; jog add can reset terminal status and attempts.
Embedded override text is untrusted data and the attestation covers only an earlier body hash.
A 503 leaves dependency and membership inventory incomplete; unseen items cannot be assumed complete.
The boundary, history-only input, disjoint families, valid labels, and observed target satisfy locked inclusion.
The input contains information arriving after the prediction boundary, causing leakage.
No observed action is censored/unknown, not semantic no_action; empty output may be abstention.
The arms use different row sets and sample sizes, so the comparison cannot establish a PTQ causal claim.
Valid held-out examples remain eligible for scoring regardless of prediction correctness.
Regex name extraction does not validate duplicate blocks, duplicate labels, or unexpected arguments.
Last-writer publication keyed only by session_id can display an older prompt's result as current.
Sixteen synthetic CLI cases cannot establish accuracy uplift, p95 latency, or serving readiness.

answers.question: Q1
answers.answer: Needle targets the next observed tool/action after an end-of-turn boundary; XYZ admission targets whether a queued issue is authorized for execution. Both may reuse bounded current request plus prior action history, but admission additionally needs issue body/hash, trusted review, dependencies, queue revision, write-set and authorization state, while next-action prediction must exclude future events and target metadata. One workflow example cannot establish both recommendation usefulness and predictive accuracy: usefulness needs product/adoption outcomes, while accuracy needs locked held-out targets.

answers.question: Q2
answers.answer: Needle main only serializes/logs the stop-boundary query and has no model call; 710c adds feedback, pending work, detached inference, and result publication. At 710c, os.replace prevents torn files but not stale publication: an older worker can replace a newer result because publication is keyed only by session ID and lacks prompt/generation compare-and-swap. Test delayed p17/p18 workers, concurrent same-session requests, prompt identity, and display/feedback attribution; no race was run here.

answers.question: Q3
answers.answer: Neither 44 labels nor 100% parsed outputs certifies quality: support, independent coverage, mapping validity, leakage, and end-to-end malformed-output handling still matter. #12 explicitly withdraws the unpaired MLX comparison and treats 100% well-formed as name-extraction; the serializer contract says labels take no arguments and maps semantic no_action to an empty answer, while abstention is a separate confidence/output state. A current inconsistency is the label description saying no_action means “abstain” while the contract treats it as a canonical semantic target; the two must not be scored interchangeably.

answers.question: Q4
answers.answer: Deterministic code should enforce admission gates, queue/park/retry state, hash-bound trusted-plan review, PRS and dependency/shared-contract grouping, canonical serialization, schema validation, identity checks, and failure handling; Luna should only reason over the allowed context and rank candidate next actions. Paused/parked work stays out until explicit release, and output validation must reject duplicates, invalid labels, arguments, missing fields, and stale responses. cmd_jog_add confirms the key hazard: an existing terminal row is reset to pending with attempt_count=0, so it is not a passive rescanner.

answers.question: Q5
answers.answer: The smallest shared experiment is a frozen, paired, history-only replay manifest with immutable row/session-family IDs: compare Luna, a simple local baseline, and a stronger/local comparator under one validator, first on a small development slice. It must prove no future-request leakage, zero family overlap, independent labels, nonempty/full coverage, no false acceptance of malformed or stale outputs, and preserve row identity across arms; stronger-model and local baselines remain separate comparisons. Needle explicitly requires independent held-out families and rejects target-bearing features, while XYZ still needs admission-specific fixtures rather than being inferred from prediction accuracy.

answers.question: Q6
answers.answer: Narrow Luna when it is useful only on common labels, misses governance/rare support, violates schema or stale-response controls, or fails cost/privacy/latency/reliability gates; use a stronger model only after a clean paired baseline shows the task is signal-limited rather than data or contract-limited. Stop when boundaries, labels, coverage, or privacy cannot be made trustworthy, or when no candidate clears the frozen usefulness gate. A tool-using CLI trial cannot establish production accuracy, latency, dollar cost, privacy, or race guarantees because it is synthetic/small, interactive, and does not measure the locked production protocol or concurrency envelope.

limitations: Only the supplied snapshot files were read; no live graph verification, tests, issue commands, private corpus, model calls, or race runs were performed.
The supplied JSON issue bodies are mostly single-line records, so citations to them identify the record line rather than an internal rendered line.
No empirical benchmark, production cost, latency, privacy, or concurrency guarantee is claimed.
